edits.find: In every vaccine series, do not restart and do not repeat; after a gap, resume where you left off ·
edits.with: An interrupted vaccine series is not restarted; resume where you left off. A dose given 5 or more days before the minimum interval does not count and is repeated ·
edits.note: PENDING s33: pearl contradicted the "Repeat the second dose" item. CDC General Best Practice, Timing and Spacing (opened 2026-10-03): "Doses of any vaccine administered >=5 days earlier than the minimum interval or age should not be counted as valid doses and should be repeated"; "an interruption in the vaccination schedule does not require restarting the entire series".

edits.with: and is preferred. Where primary HPV testing is not available, co-testing every 5 years or cytology alone every 3 years remains acceptable.
edits.note: PENDING s33: ACS 2020 still accepts cotesting and cytology alone. cancer.org ACS cervical screening guideline (opened 2026-10-03): "Co-testing, every 5 years"; "Pap test alone, every 3 years: If none of the other approaches are an option".

edits.find: HIV — start within 1 year of sexual debut, the one exception to never screening before 21. Screen with cytology annually for 3 years, then every 3 years;
edits.with: HIV — start at 21, as for everyone else, or at HIV diagnosis if older (HHS (Department of Health and Human Services) 2024 and ASCCP (American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology)); the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) 2021 STI (sexually transmitted infection) guideline instead screens 1 year after sexual debut, no later than 21 ⚠︎. Screen with cytology annually for 3 years, then every 3 years;
edits.note: PENDING s33 (check start ages): HHS adult/adolescent OI guideline, HPV (updated 2024-07-09, opened 2026-10-03): under 21 "No screening recommended"; "cervical cancer screening is recommended to start at age 21"; 21-29 "Cytology yearly. If normal cytology on 3 consecutive annual tests, adjust to every 3 years". ASCCP patient resource Feb 2026: people with HIV "should start screening at age 21 even if they were infected before this age". CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021 (opened 2026-10-03): "Adolescents with HIV should be screened 1 year after onset of sexual activity but no later than age 21 years." Conflict labelled.

edits.find: Progression to cancer takes more than a decade. Early screening finds transient infection and leads to excisional procedures (LEEP) that raise preterm-birth risk in women who were never going to develop cancer. Cervical cancer under 21 is therefore rare. Screening her would cause harm without benefit.
edits.with: Progression to cancer takes more than a decade, so cervical cancer under 21 is rare. Early screening finds transient infection and leads to excisional procedures (LEEP) that raise preterm-birth risk in women who were never going to develop cancer. Screening her would cause harm without benefit.
edits.note: PENDING s33: rarity follows clearance and slow progression, not the screening harm. Reorder only; no fact changed.

edits.find: Exit ramps: where the age floor moves HIV infection → screen at diagnosis (or within 1 year of sexual debut if younger), then annually × 3, then every 3 years. This is the one exception that starts screening before age 21 · other immunocompromise (transplant, chronic steroids) → same accelerated schedule ·
edits.with: Exit ramps: where the schedule changes HIV infection → start at 21, or at diagnosis if older, then annually × 3, then every 3 years (HHS (Department of Health and Human Services) 2024, ASCCP (American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology)). The CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) 2021 STI guideline instead screens 1 year after sexual debut, no later than 21 ⚠︎ · other immunocompromise (organ or allogeneic stem cell transplant, immunosuppressed inflammatory bowel disease) → start at 21, then the same accelerated schedule ·
edits.note: PENDING s33: "the one exception" conflicted with the next row; non-HIV start age checked. ASCCP patient resource Feb 2026 (opened 2026-10-03): "People with an organ transplant, allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant ..., or inflammatory bowel disease on immunosuppressant medications ... should begin cervical cancer screening with the pap test at age 21." Moscicki 2019 update (PMC11939099): follow CDC HIV screening guidelines for SOT, ESRD, HSCT, SLE. HIV sources as in the cervical edit. "chronic steroids" replaced by the ASCCP-named groups.

edits.with: Drug-Induced Immune Hemolysis also brings hemolysis labs and dark urine, but the cause is immune: spherocytes and a positive direct antiglobulin test, not schistocytes. Ask: is there a mechanical source?

edits.find: A live divergence worth knowing As of January 2026 the CDC schedule specifies one HPV dose at 11 to 12 while the AAP recommends two doses at 9 to 12. On retired exam items, the classic keyed answer remains two doses if initiated before 15 and three if at 15 or older or immunocompromised. Expect the exam answer to lag clinical practice here.
edits.with: Schedule status, October 2026 A January 2026 CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) revision recommended a single HPV dose. A federal court stayed that revision in March 2026, and the stay is under appeal. The schedule CDC now posts keeps the 2-dose series when started at 9 to 14, and the AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) also recommends two doses, starting at 9 to 12; check the CDC site for the current schedule. On retired exam items, the classic keyed answer remains two doses if initiated before 15 and three if at 15 or older or immunocompromised. The posted schedule and the exam answer currently agree.
edits.note: PENDING s35: the "live divergence" line was outdated by the court stay. Society of Gynecologic Oncology (opened 2026-10-03): HPV "now recommended as a single dose" under the January 2026 schedule. Georgetown CCF 2026-03-31: the court "stayed the January 2026 Memo revising the CDC childhood immunization schedule" (2026-03-16). Moreton 2026-09-17: government appealed to the First Circuit. CDC child-adolescent notes (opened 2026-10-03, last updated 2025-07-01): "2-dose series at 0, 6-12 months" for initiation at 9-14. AAP two-dose wording carried from the existing line.
